report_md:
# Gap continuation: development report

**Family:** `gap-continuation` (new). Primary mechanism: a large opening gap
plus first-30-minute confirmation continues through the session.

**Verdict: positive and robust, but below the program's 36.72% above-TQQQ CAGR
bar. It passes every integrity/robustness gate and is a genuine risk-adjusted
diversifier (Sharpe 0.94, max DD 15.5%, correlation <= 0.32 to every current
winner), not an above-TQQQ replacement.**

Development window 2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29, 1-minute marks, next-open fills,
2% band, long-only, weights >= 0, sum <= 1. The panel is requested with
`end=2023-12-29`; no 2024-2026 bar is used. The only data inputs are the
shared QQQ/TQQQ/BIL panel; the signal itself uses QQQ open/close, and the
position is TQQQ.

---

## 1. Headline

| | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Sortino | Vol | TQQQ weight (bar-time) | Fills | Turnover | Ending equity |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **Primary, 1 bp** | **11.25%** | **15.45%** | **0.94** | **1.34** | 12.2% | 6.96% | 304 | 533x | $234,250 |
| Primary, 2 bp | 10.83% | 15.59% | 0.91 | 1.29 | 12.2% | 6.96% | 304 | 524x | $227,236 |
| Primary, 5 bp | 9.57% | 16.38% | 0.81 | 1.16 | 12.2% | 6.96% | 304 | 497x | $207,429 |
| Primary, 10 bp | 7.50% | 17.83% | 0.66 | 0.93 | 12.2% | 6.96% | 304 | 456x | $178,179 |
| Primary, 0 bp (gross) | 11.67% | 15.32% | 0.97 | 1.38 | 12.2% | 6.96% | 304 | 543x | $241,480 |
| TQQQ buy & hold (sim) | 36.15% | 82.29% | 0.80 | 1.12 | 66.5% | 100% | 1 | 1x | $1,175,165 |
| TQQQ bar from the brief | 36.72% | 82.29% | 0.82 | -- | -- | 100% | -- | -- | -- |

- The strategy is **25.5 pp below** the TQQQ CAGR bar at 1 bp. It is **not**
  an above-TQQQ replacement.
- It cuts max drawdown by **66.8 pp** (15.45% vs 82.29%) and raises Sharpe
  from 0.80 to 0.94. Sortino is 1.34 vs 1.12. The risk-adjusted profile is
  better than TQQQ even though the absolute return is lower.
- Cost sensitivity is mild: 5 bp costs 1.68 pp of CAGR, 10 bp costs 3.75 pp.
  The 5 bp and 10 bp results remain positive. Turnover is 533x initial equity
  over 8 years (~67x/yr), low because the book is flat most of the time.
- Exposure is **6.96% of 1-minute bars** and **1.88% of clock time** (152
  events x 358 held minutes / (2012 sessions x 1440)). The rest is cash at 0%.
- Daily correlation to TQQQ is **0.290**. This is a small, separate intraday
  sleeve, not a leveraged beta clone.
- Max drawdown episode: **2023-06-30 -> 2023-11-29, 15.45%**. This is also the
  main warning: 2023 was -13.9% and the 2022-23 subperiod CAGR is only 3.49%.

---

## 2. What it is

Universe: QQQ (signal), TQQQ (position), cash.

At the close of the 10:00 bar:

```
gap_k = QQQ_open(09:30) / QQQ_close(previous 15:59) - 1
r30_k = QQQ_close(10:00) / QQQ_open(09:30) - 1
```

If `gap_k >= +0.50%` and `r30_k >= +0.20%`, buy TQQQ at the **10:01 open**.
Sell at the **15:59 open**. Otherwise hold cash. No overnight position in the
primary rule.

**Clock.** The gap is known at 09:30. The confirmation is the 10:00 bar close.
The decision is taken at 10:00:00; the fill is the next bar open at 10:01. The
exit is decided at the 15:58 close and filled at the 15:59 open. There is no
same-bar fill. The previous close is the prior session's 15:59 close, so the
gap uses only completed data.

Only 390-bar sessions are traded. Half-days and short sessions are skipped;
they still update the previous close. This is a data-quality rule.

---

## 3. Why the signal, not just the calendar

The event sample is 152 trades over 8 years, **19.0 events/year**. Per-event
gross return, entry 10:01 open to exit 15:59 open:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Events | 152 |
| Mean | **+62.6 bp** |
| Median | +85.3 bp |
| Win rate | 64.5% |
| t-stat | **2.59** |
| Worst | -988 bp |
| Best | +1,358 bp |
| Sum of log returns | +0.882 |

The positive mean is not a single outlier: the median is higher than the mean,
and the win rate is 64.5%. The worst event (-9.9% on TQQQ) is a real gap-day
risk and is the reason the strategy needs the 15:59 exit rather than an
overnight hold.

The controls separate the two legs:

| Control | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Fills | What it says |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Gap only, **no** confirmation | 7.38% | 37.27% | 0.42 | 844 | The gap alone is weak and much riskier. |
| Confirmation only, **no** gap | 20.11% | 33.96% | 0.82 | 1,276 | The first-30-minute drive alone is a different, stronger-return / much-riskier trade. |
| Gap up, first 30m **down** (fade) | -0.28% | 35.08% | 0.08 | 382 | Fading the gap does not work in this sample. |
| Buy & hold TQQQ | 36.15% | 82.29% | 0.80 | 1 | The absolute-return bar. |

The gap filter is therefore a **risk selector**, not the whole return source:
it halves the confirmation-only CAGR but cuts its drawdown from 34.0% to
15.5% and raises Sharpe from 0.82 to 0.94. The family's claim is that the
*combination* is the trade; the report does not claim that the gap alone
carries the return.

---

## 4. Robustness

### 4.1 Pre-registered grid (8 cells)

All cells use the 10:01 -> 15:59 clock and TQQQ 1.0. The centre is cell 4.

| Cell | Gap | r30 | 1 bp CAGR | 1 bp DD | 1 bp Sharpe | 5 bp CAGR | Fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.30% | 0.00% | 6.38% | 34.34% | 0.44 | 2.69% | 706 |
| 2 | 0.30% | 0.20% | 10.84% | 20.15% | 0.82 | 8.41% | 442 |
| 3 | 0.50% | 0.00% | 7.68% | 25.20% | 0.58 | 5.22% | 462 |
| **4** | **0.50%** | **0.20%** | **11.25%** | **15.45%** | **0.94** | **9.57%** | **304** |
| 5 | 0.75% | 0.00% | 5.26% | 24.59% | 0.47 | 3.85% | 270 |
| 6 | 0.75% | 0.20% | 9.33% | 15.36% | 0.90 | 8.35% | 180 |
| 7 | 1.00% | 0.00% | 3.27% | 29.22% | 0.35 | 2.40% | 170 |
| 8 | 1.00% | 0.20% | 8.50% | 17.80% | 0.96 | 7.85% | 120 |

**8/8 cells are positive at 1 bp and 8/8 at 5 bp.** The 1 bp CAGR range is
3.27% to 11.25%; the centre is the best cell, but cell 8 has the highest
Sharpe (0.96) with only 60 events. The plateau is broad in sign, not in level.
The monotone pattern (confirmation always helps; a larger gap lowers CAGR but
also lowers drawdown) is economically consistent, not a random ridge.

### 4.2 Neighbours (not used to choose the centre)

| Neighbour | 1 bp CAGR | 1 bp DD | Sharpe | 5 bp CAGR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Gap 0.40% | 10.97% | 14.51% | 0.88 | 8.93% |
| Gap 0.60% | 8.43% | 15.84% | 0.77 | 7.11% |
| r30 0.10% | 9.31% | 20.65% | 0.74 | 7.28% |
| r30 0.30% | 7.79% | 12.14% | 0.80 | 6.62% |
| r30 0.50% | 5.80% | 14.50% | 0.77 | 5.24% |
| Entry 10:16 | 9.28% | 15.69% | 0.81 | 7.63% |
| Entry 10:31 | 6.82% | 13.98% | 0.64 | 5.20% |
| Entry 11:01 | 7.83% | 15.92% | 0.76 | 6.20% |
| Exit 15:30 | 11.26% | 15.29% | 0.99 | 9.58% |
| Exit 15:45 | 11.79% | 15.41% | 1.01 | 10.10% |
| **Next-open exit** | **15.69%** | **20.22%** | **0.95** | **13.94%** |
| Size 0.50 | 5.71% | 7.96% | 0.94 | 4.91% |
| QQQ execution | 3.80% | 5.59% | 0.92 | 2.23% |
| TQQQ signal 1.5%/0.5% | 10.85% | 17.06% | 0.89 | 9.06% |

The result is stable to the entry minute and the signal asset. The
next-open exit is stronger in CAGR (15.69%) and keeps Sharpe at 0.95, but it
adds overnight risk and overlaps the session-timing family. It is reported as
a neighbour, not promoted, to keep this family a pure intraday continuation
trade. The QQQ execution has a lower CAGR but the same Sharpe (0.92) and a
much lower drawdown (5.59%), confirming that the signal is in QQQ and TQQQ is
mainly a capital-efficiency choice.

### 4.3 Placebos

| Placebo | Draws | Real CAGR | Placebo mean | Placebo p95 | Max | p-value | Real DD percentile |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Random days, same count, 10:01 -> 15:59 | 200 | 11.25% | -0.25% | 5.67% | 11.89% | **0.005** | 99.5% |
| Random entry 10:01-10:30, same signal days | 200 | 11.25% | 9.25% | 10.28% | 10.89% | **0.000** | 15.5% |
| Stale signal (previous session) | 1 | 11.25% | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |

- The random-day placebo is the strong result: random calendar days with the
  same clock average -0.25% CAGR and only 5.67% at the 95th percentile. The
  real result is at the 99.5th percentile and its drawdown is better than
  99.5% of random-day draws. The gap/confirmation signal is selecting the
  days, not riding calendar drift.
- The random-entry placebo is weaker evidence. The real 11.25% beats all 200
  random-entry draws (max 10.89%), p=0.000, but the mean random entry still
  earns 9.25%. The 10:01 timing adds about 2.0 pp of CAGR, not the whole
  edge. The real drawdown is *worse* than 84.5% of random-entry draws (15.45%
  vs a 14.65% mean), so the early entry is a return choice, not a drawdown
  reducer.
- The stale signal loses money (-3.64% CAGR, -42.7% DD), so the same-day gap
  and confirmation are doing the work.

### 4.4 Subperiods and yearly

| Period | CAGR | Max DD |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2016-2019 | 10.61% | 14.77% |
| 2020-2021 | 20.10% | 14.51% |
| 2022-2023 | **3.49%** | 15.45% |

| Year | Strategy | TQQQ |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2016 | +9.17% | +19.86% |
| 2017 | +7.59% | +114.54% |
| 2018 | +19.29% | -20.76% |
| 2019 | +6.71% | +148.23% |
| 2020 | +25.95% | +104.14% |
| 2021 | +16.21% | +81.05% |
| 2022 | +24.31% | -79.39% |
| 2023 | **-13.89%** | +192.05% |

The strategy is positive in 7 of 8 calendar years and in all three
subperiods, but 2023 is a clear loss and the 2022-23 CAGR is only 3.49%. The
2023 drawdown is the current max-DD episode. The cut tests (excluding one year
at a time) range from 9.30% to 15.40% CAGR, so no single year carries the
result, but excluding 2023 *raises* CAGR to 15.40% — the 2023 loss is a real
drag, not a hidden dependency.

| Cut | Strategy CAGR | Strategy DD | TQQQ ex-year CAGR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ex-2016 | 11.55% | 14.91% | 38.66% |
| ex-2017 | 11.79% | 14.91% | 27.06% |
| ex-2018 | 10.14% | 14.91% | 46.60% |
| ex-2019 | 11.92% | 14.91% | 25.90% |
| ex-2020 | 9.30% | 14.91% | 27.84% |
| ex-2021 | 10.56% | 14.91% | 30.34% |
| ex-2022 | 9.50% | 14.91% | 77.75% |
| ex-2023 | 15.40% | 10.10% | 21.49% |

---

## 5. Correlation to the nine current winners

Daily returns, 2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29, 2,011 overlapping days.

| Winner | Correlation |
|---|---:|
| ratio-froth | 0.097 |
| vol-scaled-crash-stop | 0.213 |
| relative-value-tqqq | 0.220 |
| fomc-opex-window | 0.178 |
| family-session-timing | 0.147 |
| family-short-reversal | 0.282 |
| family-rebalance-flow | 0.223 |
| family-intraday-microstructure-day | **0.318** |
| family-ml-microstructure | 0.227 |

Range **0.097 .. 0.318**, well below the 0.70 independence gate. The highest
correlation is with `family-intraday-microstructure-day` (0.318), which also
trades a first-30-minute signal; the overlap is real but small because this
family waits for 10:01 and requires a large gap. It is not a duplicate.

---

## 6. Kill criteria

| Criterion | Value | Failed? |
|---|---:|---|
| 1 bp CAGR below 36.72% TQQQ bar | 11.25% | **FAIL** |
| 5 bp CAGR below 0 | 9.57% | pass |
| Fewer than 30 independent events | 152 | pass |
| Fewer than 100 fills | 304 | pass |
| Fewer than 6/8 grid cells positive at 1 bp | 8/8 | pass |
| Negative CAGR in 2+ of 3 subperiods | 0 of 3 | pass |
| Placebo random-day p-value > 0.10 | 0.005 | pass |
| Correlation > 0.70 with a winner | 0.318 | pass |
| Weight drift before a truncation cut | 0.0 | pass |

**Only the absolute-return bar fails.** The strategy is honest about that: it
is not an above-TQQQ strategy. It is a low-exposure, low-drawdown,
near-uncorrelated intraday sleeve with a statistically meaningful event mean
(t = 2.59) and a placebo result that random days do not reproduce.

---

## 7. Risks and limitations

1. **2023 decay.** The 2023 result is -13.9%, and 2022-23 CAGR is 3.49%. The
   effect may be weakening as gap continuation becomes more widely traded, or
   2023 may be a single bad year. The development window cannot distinguish
   these; the honest read is that the recent edge is thin.
2. **Long-only asymmetry.** The book cannot trade gap-down continuation. The
   measured effect may be symmetric in reality; this strategy only harvests
   the long half.
3. **Event concentration.** 152 events, 19/year. The t-stat is 2.59, but a
   handful of large gap days carry a meaningful share of the return (best
   +13.6%, worst -9.9%).
4. **Gap definition.** The gap uses the previous 15:59 close, not an official
   opening auction print. The 09:30 open in the 1-minute archive is the first
   regular-session trade; this is the correct causal input for this panel.
5. **Execution.** TQQQ at the 10:01 and 15:59 opens with a 2% band. The 5 bp
   and 10 bp columns show the strategy survives plausible costs, but a real
   implementation also faces borrow/locate and market-impact costs that the
   flat-bps model does not capture.

## 8. Verdict

**Fail on the program's above-TQQQ CAGR bar; pass on activity, cost stress,
plateau, subperiods, placebo, independence and causality.** The gap and
first-30-minute confirmation select a real continuation event (+62.6 bp mean,
t = 2.59). The best honest description is a small, diversifying intraday
sleeve, not a replacement for TQQQ. If the program only promotes
above-TQQQ strategies, this family should stay in the research archive. If it
also values low-drawdown, near-uncorrelated sleeves, this is the strongest of
the four new families.
hypothesis_md:
# Gap continuation: hypothesis and pre-registration

**Family:** `gap-continuation` (new). This is a *continuation* family, not a
gap fade.

**One-line hypothesis.** A large opening gap is a repricing of information.
When the first 30 minutes confirm the direction of the gap, the repricing is
incomplete and the move continues through the session. A gap that is not
confirmed is a different event and is not traded.

**Development window.** 2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29 only. The shared 1-minute
panel is requested with `end=2023-12-29`; no 2024-2026 bar enters any signal,
weight or statistic. The holdout is not loaded for design.

---

## 1. Why this should exist

The gap is the market's first public estimate of overnight information. If the
estimate is correct, the first 30 minutes should trade in the gap direction as
the rest of the market adjusts. If the gap is a liquidity overreaction, the
first 30 minutes should fail and the gap should fade. These are opposite
trades. The family tests the continuation side only, because the book is
long-only.

The signal is deliberately *not*:

- a short-term reversal (the previous day's close-to-open move is the input,
  and the trade is in the same direction);
- an opening-range breakout (the trigger is the 10:00 close versus the 09:30
  open, not a range boundary);
- a trend gate, volatility target, drawdown event, ML model or
  relative-strength input.

## 2. Exact rules

All times are US/Eastern. Bar offsets are 0-based from 09:30 (offset 0) to
15:59 (offset 389). A weight set after bar `i` fills at bar `i+1`'s open.

| Item | Rule |
|---|---|
| Signal asset | QQQ |
| Trade asset | TQQQ (3x QQQ), weight 1.0, cash otherwise |
| Gap | `QQQ_open(09:30) / QQQ_close(previous 15:59) - 1` |
| Confirmation | `QQQ_close(10:00) / QQQ_open(09:30) - 1` |
| Entry | `gap >= +0.50%` **and** `r30 >= +0.20%`; buy at the **10:01 open** |
| Exit | sell at the **15:59 open** (target zero at the 15:58 close) |
| Hold | 10:01 open through 15:58 close = 358 minutes |
| Overnight | flat; the next-open exit is a neighbour, not the primary |
| Short side | not traded (long-only book); gap-down continuation is out of scope |

**Decision clock.** The gap is known at 09:30. The confirmation is the close
of the 10:00 bar. The decision is taken at 10:00:00, after that close, and the
fill is the next bar's open at 10:01. There is no same-bar fill and no use of
the 10:01 bar in the signal. The exit is decided at the 15:58 close and filled
at the 15:59 open.

**Session filter.** Only sessions with 390 one-minute bars are traded. Short
and half sessions are skipped; they are still used to update the previous
close. This is a data-quality rule, not a regime filter.

## 3. Pre-registered centre and grid

Centre: **gap >= 0.50% QQQ, r30 >= 0.20%, 10:01 -> 15:59, TQQQ 1.0.**

The 8-cell grid varies the two economic thresholds and holds the clock fixed:

| Cell | Gap | r30 |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.30% | 0.00% |
| 2 | 0.30% | 0.20% |
| 3 | 0.50% | 0.00% |
| 4 | **0.50%** | **0.20%** (centre) |
| 5 | 0.75% | 0.00% |
| 6 | 0.75% | 0.20% |
| 7 | 1.00% | 0.00% |
| 8 | 1.00% | 0.20% |

The centre is chosen because 0.50% QQQ is roughly a 1.5% TQQQ gap, a visibly
large overnight repricing, and 0.20% is a first-30-minute move that is large
enough not to be one-tick noise. It is not chosen by scanning the return
surface; the grid is reported in full and the centre is allowed to be
non-best.

## 4. Primary bar and kill criteria (stated before results)

Primary performance is the 1 bp headline. The strategy must also survive
5 bp and 10 bp. A candidate is **killed** if any of the following holds:

1. Dev CAGR at 1 bp is below the 36.72% TQQQ development bar.
2. 5 bp CAGR is below zero (cost-fragile).
3. Fewer than 30 independent events or fewer than 100 fills (dead strategy).
4. Fewer than 6 of the 8 grid cells have positive 1 bp CAGR (parameter
   fragility).
5. Negative CAGR in 2 or more of the 3 subperiods (2016-19, 2020-21,
   2022-23).
6. Placebo random-day p-value above 0.10 (the signal does not beat random
   timing).
7. Daily-return correlation above 0.70 with any of the nine current winners
   (not independent).
8. Any weight drift before a truncation cut (look-ahead).

Criterion 1 is the program's absolute-return bar. Criteria 2-8 are robustness
and integrity gates. A strategy can pass 2-8 and still fail 1; that is reported
as a risk-adjusted pass, not as an above-TQQQ replacement.

## 5. Placebos

- **Random days:** draw the same number of full sessions at random, keep the
  10:01 -> 15:59 clock. 200 draws. This asks whether the gap/confirmation
  signal selects better days than the calendar.
- **Random entry:** keep the signal days, move the entry uniformly over
  10:01-10:30, keep the 15:59 exit. 200 draws. This asks whether 10:01 is the
  right moment.
- **Stale signal:** use the previous session's gap and confirmation flags.
  This asks whether the same-day signal is doing the work.
- **Controls:** gap-only (no confirmation), confirmation-only (no gap), and
  gap-up with a down first 30 minutes (the fade). These separate the two legs
  of the signal.

## 6. What would falsify the hypothesis

- A positive gap-only or fade result as strong as the confirmed-gap result
  would mean the confirmation is not the mechanism.
- A flat or negative event mean with a t-stat near zero would mean the gap
  continuation is not present in this sample.
- A random-day placebo that matches the real result would mean the edge is
  calendar drift, not the gap.
- A 2023-only collapse with no earlier evidence would mean the effect is
  regime-specific and should not be promoted.

The report applies these tests and states which ones fired.

"""Gap-continuation TQQQ: a large gap confirmed in the first 30 minutes.

Standalone development-window strategy (2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29).

Hypothesis
----------
A large opening gap is information, not automatically an overreaction.  When
the first 30 minutes trade in the gap direction, the move continues through
the session.  This family tests *continuation*, not the gap fade.

Rules
-----
Signal, measured on QQQ at the close of the 10:00 bar (offset 30):

    gap_k  = QQQ_open(09:30) / QQQ_close(previous 15:59) - 1
    r30_k  = QQQ_close(10:00) / QQQ_open(09:30) - 1

    gap_k >= 0.50%  and  r30_k >= 0.20%   -> long TQQQ

Execution: enter at the 10:01 open (the bar after the 10:00 signal close),
exit at the 15:59 open (target zero at the 15:58 close).  Long-only, weight
1.0, cash otherwise.  No overnight position in the primary rule.

No trend gate, no volatility targeting, no drawdown event, no ML, no
relative-strength input.  The gap and the first-30-minute confirmation are the
only signals.

Run:
    $env:PYTHONPATH = "C:\\Users\\27175\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\opencode\\pylibs"
    $env:BT_THREADS = "1"
    python research/new/family-gap-continuation/strategy.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

DEV_START, DEV_END = "2016-01-04", "2023-12-29"

N_BARS = 390

# Pre-registered centre.
GAP_TH = 0.0050      # 0.50% QQQ gap = about 1.5% TQQQ
R30_TH = 0.0020      # first 30 minutes up at least 0.20%
ENTRY_OFF = 30       # 10:00 close decides; fill at 10:01
EXIT_OFF = 389       # 15:59 open

    "ratio-froth", "vol-scaled-crash-stop", "relative-value-tqqq",

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# data / signals
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def load_panel(start: str = DEV_START, end: str = DEV_END):
    return bt.panel(SYMBOLS, start, end, "1min", warmup_days=0)


def session_features(ts, o, c, sig_col: int = CQ):
    """Gap and first-30-minute return for every full session."""
    dates, first, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    n = len(first)
    gap = np.full(n, np.nan)
    r30 = np.full(n, np.nan)
    full = np.zeros(n, dtype=bool)
    prev_close = None
    for k in range(n):
        f, l = int(first[k]), int(last[k])
        if l - f == N_BARS - 1:
            full[k] = True
            r30[k] = c[f + ENTRY_OFF, sig_col] / o[f, sig_col] - 1.0
            if prev_close is not None:
                gap[k] = o[f, sig_col] / prev_close - 1.0
        prev_close = float(c[l, sig_col])
    return gap, r30, full


def build_flags(gap, r30, full, gap_th: float = GAP_TH, r30_th: float = R30_TH):
    return (full & np.isfinite(gap) & np.isfinite(r30)
            & (gap >= gap_th) & (r30 >= r30_th))


def build_weights(ts, o, c, gap_th: float = GAP_TH, r30_th: float = R30_TH,
                  entry_off: int = ENTRY_OFF, exit_off: int = EXIT_OFF,
                  sig_col: int = CQ, trade_col: int = CT, size: float = 1.0,
                  flags_override=None, entry_random: np.ndarray | None = None,
                  return_diag: bool = False):
    """Return the (n, 3) weight matrix.

    `weights[i]` is the target after bar i's close; it fills at bar i+1's
    open.  With entry_off=30 and exit_off=389 the position runs from the
    10:01 open to the 15:59 open.
    """
    dates, first, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    n = len(first)
    if flags_override is None:
        gap, r30, full = session_features(ts, o, c, sig_col)
        flags = build_flags(gap, r30, full, gap_th, r30_th)
    else:
        flags = np.asarray(flags_override, dtype=bool)
    w = np.zeros((len(ts), 3))
    for k in range(n):
        if not flags[k]:
            continue
        f, l = int(first[k]), int(last[k])
        if l - f != N_BARS - 1:
            continue
        en = f + entry_off if entry_random is None else f + int(entry_random[k])
        en = min(max(en, f + 1), f + N_BARS - 2)
        if exit_off < N_BARS:
            ex = f + exit_off
            w[en:ex - 1, trade_col] = size
            w[ex - 1, trade_col] = 0.0
        else:
            # Hold through the 15:59 close and exit at the next 09:31 open.
            w[en:f + N_BARS, trade_col] = size
            if k + 1 < n:
                w[int(first[k + 1]), trade_col] = 0.0
    w[-1] = w[-2]
    assert w.min() >= -1e-12 and w.max() <= 1.0 + 1e-12
    assert w.sum(axis=1).max() <= 1.0 + 1e-9
    if return_diag:
        return w, flags
    return w


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# evaluation helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def pack(s: dict) -> dict:
    keys = ("cagr", "max_drawdown", "sharpe", "sortino", "volatility",
            "exposure", "turnover", "fills", "ending_equity", "years")
    return {k: (int(s[k]) if k == "fills" else float(s[k])) for k in keys}


def run_weights(ts, o, c, w, start=DEV_START, slip=1.0):
    r = bt.run(ts, o, c, w, start, band=0.02, slippage_bps=slip)
    return r, bt.stats(r, BPY)


def daily_equity(res: dict) -> pd.Series:
    s = pd.Series(res["equity"], index=pd.to_datetime(res["ts"]))
    out = s.groupby(s.index.date).last()
    out.index = pd.to_datetime(out.index)
    return out


def daily_close_returns(ts, close) -> pd.Series:
    s = pd.Series(close, index=pd.to_datetime(ts))
    out = s.groupby(s.index.date).last()
    out.index = pd.to_datetime(out.index)
    return out.pct_change().dropna()


def dd_window(ts, equity):
    peak = np.maximum.accumulate(equity)
    dd = equity / peak - 1.0
    j = int(np.argmin(dd))
    i = int(np.argmax(equity[: j + 1]))
    return {"peak": str(ts[i])[:10], "trough": str(ts[j])[:10],
            "dd": float(-dd[j])}


def subperiod(ts, equity, lo, hi):
    m = ((ts >= pd.Timestamp(lo, tz="America/New_York"))
         & (ts < pd.Timestamp(hi, tz="America/New_York") + pd.Timedelta(days=1)))
    x, tt = equity[m], ts[m]
    if len(x) < 2:
        return None
    years = (tt[-1] - tt[0]).total_seconds() / (365.25 * 86400)
    peak = np.maximum.accumulate(x)
    return {"cagr": float((x[-1] / x[0]) ** (1 / years) - 1),
            "max_drawdown": float(-(x / peak - 1).min())}


def calendar_year_cut(ts, equity, year: int) -> dict:
    s = pd.Series(equity, index=pd.to_datetime(ts))
    d = s.groupby(s.index.date).last()
    d.index = pd.to_datetime(d.index)
    r = d.pct_change().dropna()
    r = r[np.array([x.year != year for x in r.index])]
    eq = np.cumprod(1.0 + r.to_numpy())
    years = len(r) / 252.0
    peak = np.maximum.accumulate(eq)
    return {"cagr": float(eq[-1] ** (1 / years) - 1),
            "max_drawdown": float(-(eq / peak - 1).min()),
            "years": float(years)}


def event_stats(ts, o, c, flags, trade_col=CT, entry_off=ENTRY_OFF,
                exit_off=EXIT_OFF):
    dates, first, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    rets = []
    for k in np.flatnonzero(flags):
        f = int(first[k])
        if int(last[k]) - f != N_BARS - 1:
            continue
        rets.append(o[f + exit_off, trade_col] / o[f + entry_off + 1, trade_col] - 1.0)
    r = np.array(rets)
    return {
        "n_events": int(len(r)),
        "events_per_year": float(len(r) / 7.98),
        "mean_bp": float(1e4 * r.mean()) if len(r) else None,
        "median_bp": float(1e4 * np.median(r)) if len(r) else None,
        "win_rate": float((r > 0).mean()) if len(r) else None,
        "t_stat": float(r.mean() / r.std() * np.sqrt(len(r))) if len(r) > 1 else None,
        "worst_bp": float(1e4 * r.min()) if len(r) else None,
        "best_bp": float(1e4 * r.max()) if len(r) else None,
        "total_log": float(np.log1p(r).sum()) if len(r) else None,
    }


def correlation_table(daily_ret: pd.Series) -> dict:
    out = {}
    for slug in WINNERS:
        path = ROOT / "research" / "new" / "curves" / f"{slug}.json"
        if not path.exists():
            continue
        d = json.loads(path.read_text())
        ser = pd.Series(d["values"], index=pd.to_datetime(d["dates"]))
        ser = ser[ser.index <= pd.Timestamp(DEV_END)]
        j = pd.concat([daily_ret, ser.pct_change()], axis=1, join="inner").dropna()
        out[slug] = {"corr": float(j.iloc[:, 0].corr(j.iloc[:, 1])),
                     "n_days": int(len(j))}
    return out

# main
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def main():
    ts, o, c = load_panel()
    print(f"panel {len(ts):,} bars, {len(np.unique(ts.date))} sessions, "
          f"{ts[0].date()} .. {ts[-1].date()}")

    w, flags = build_weights(ts, o, c, return_diag=True)
    wraw = np.zeros((len(ts), 3))
    wraw[:, CT] = 1.0

    out = {
        "strategy": "gap-continuation-tqqq",
        "directory": "research/new/family-gap-continuation",
        "window": {
            "start": DEV_START, "end": DEV_END, "marks": "1min",
            "fills": "next-minute open, 2% band", "idle": "cash (0%)",
            "holdout": "not loaded; panel sliced at 2023-12-29",
        },
        "data_provenance": {
            "panel": "research/bt.py bt.panel(('QQQ','TQQQ','BIL'), dev window, '1min')",
            "extra": "none; gap and r30 come from the shared panel",
            "no_2024": "the returned panel ends 2023-12-29 15:59 ET; no 2024 bar is used",
        },
        "rules": {
            "signal": "QQQ gap >= 0.50% and QQQ 09:30-10:00 return >= 0.20%",
            "entry": "10:01 open (decision at the 10:00 close)",
            "exit": "15:59 open (target zero at the 15:58 close)",
            "instrument": "TQQQ, weight 1.0",
            "no": "trend gate, volatility target, drawdown event, ML, relative strength",
        },
        "event_stats": event_stats(ts, o, c, flags),
        "dev": {},
    }

    results = {}
    for slip in (0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 5.0, 10.0):
        res, s = run_weights(ts, o, c, w, slip=slip)
        results[slip] = (res, s)
        key = "gross_0bp" if slip == 0.0 else f"{int(slip)}bp"
        out["dev"][key] = pack(s)
        print(f"centre {slip:4.1f}bp  CAGR {s['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  DD {s['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%  "
              f"Sharpe {s['sharpe']:4.2f}  Sortino {s['sortino']:4.2f}  vol {s['volatility']*100:5.1f}%  "
              f"expo {s['exposure']*100:5.2f}%  fills {s['fills']:,}  turnover {s['turnover']:.0f}")

    res1, s1 = results[1.0]
    i0 = bt.start_index(ts, DEV_START)
    bench = bt.benchmark(c[i0:, CT], ts[i0:], BPY)
    out["benchmark_tqqq_sim"] = {k: float(v) for k, v in bench.items()}
    out["benchmark_tqqq_brief"] = {"cagr": 0.3672, "max_drawdown": 0.8229,
                                   "sharpe": 0.82,
                                   "note": "brief's official dev bar, daily-close marks"}

    # Exposure: bar-time and clock-time.
    held_minutes = EXIT_OFF - (ENTRY_OFF + 1)   # 10:01..15:58
    n_events = int(flags.sum())
    out["exposure"] = {
        "bar_time_mean_weight": float(np.mean(w[:, CT])),
        "bar_time_held_fraction": float(np.mean(w[:, CT] > 0)),
        "clock_time_held_frac": float(n_events * held_minutes / (len(flags) * 1440.0)),
        "held_minutes_per_event": int(held_minutes),
        "n_events": n_events,
        "events_per_year": float(n_events / 7.98),
        "mean_size": 1.0,
    }

    out["corr_daily_tqqq"] = float(
        daily_equity(res1).pct_change().corr(daily_close_returns(ts, c[:, CT])))
    out["correlations"] = correlation_table(daily_equity(res1).pct_change())

    out["yearly"] = {
        str(k): {"strategy": float(v["strategy"]), "benchmark": float(v["benchmark"])}
        for k, v in bt.yearly(res1["ts"], res1["equity"], c[i0:, CT]).items()
    }
    out["dd_window"] = dd_window(res1["ts"], res1["equity"])
    out["subperiods"] = {
        "2016_2019": subperiod(res1["ts"], res1["equity"], "2016-01-04", "2019-12-31"),
        "2020_2021": subperiod(res1["ts"], res1["equity"], "2020-01-02", "2021-12-31"),
        "2022_2023": subperiod(res1["ts"], res1["equity"], "2022-01-03", "2023-12-29"),
    }

    # ---- pre-registered grid (8 cells) --------------------------------------
    grid_specs = []
    for gth in (0.0030, 0.0050, 0.0075, 0.0100):
        for rth in (0.0, 0.0020):
            grid_specs.append((gth, rth))
    grid = []
    for gth, rth in grid_specs:
        wt = build_weights(ts, o, c, gap_th=gth, r30_th=rth)
        row = {"cell": f"gap {gth*100:.2f}% / r30 {rth*100:.2f}%",
               "gap_th": gth, "r30_th": rth,
               "centre": bool(abs(gth - GAP_TH) < 1e-12 and abs(rth - R30_TH) < 1e-12)}
        for slip in (1.0, 5.0):
            _, ss = run_weights(ts, o, c, wt, slip=slip)
            row[f"{int(slip)}bp"] = pack(ss)
        grid.append(row)
        print(f"grid {row['cell']:34s} 1bp {row['1bp']['cagr']*100:6.2f}% / "
              f"{row['1bp']['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%  Sh {row['1bp']['sharpe']:.2f}  "
              f"5bp {row['5bp']['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  fills {row['1bp']['fills']:,}")
    out["grid"] = grid

    # ---- neighbours ---------------------------------------------------------
    neigh = []

    def add_neigh(name, **kw):
        wt = build_weights(ts, o, c, **kw)
        _, ss = run_weights(ts, o, c, wt, slip=1.0)
        _, s5 = run_weights(ts, o, c, wt, slip=5.0)
        _, s10 = run_weights(ts, o, c, wt, slip=10.0)
        neigh.append({"name": name, **pack(ss),
                      "5bp_cagr": float(s5["cagr"]), "5bp_dd": float(s5["max_drawdown"]),
                      "10bp_cagr": float(s10["cagr"])})
        print(f"neigh {name:30s} 1bp {ss['cagr']*100:6.2f}% / {ss['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%  "
              f"Sh {ss['sharpe']:4.2f}  5bp {s5['cagr']*100:6.2f}%")

    add_neigh("gap 0.40%", gap_th=0.0040)
    add_neigh("gap 0.60%", gap_th=0.0060)
    add_neigh("r30 0.10%", r30_th=0.0010)
    add_neigh("r30 0.30%", r30_th=0.0030)
    add_neigh("r30 0.50%", r30_th=0.0050)
    add_neigh("entry 10:16", entry_off=45)
    add_neigh("entry 10:31", entry_off=60)
    add_neigh("entry 11:01", entry_off=90)
    add_neigh("exit 15:30", exit_off=360)
    add_neigh("exit 15:45", exit_off=375)
    add_neigh("next-open exit", exit_off=390)
    add_neigh("size 0.50", size=0.5)
    add_neigh("QQQ trade", trade_col=CQ)
    add_neigh("TQQQ signal 1.5%/0.5%", sig_col=CT, gap_th=0.015, r30_th=0.005)
    out["neighbours"] = neigh

    # ---- controls -----------------------------------------------------------
    controls = {}

    def add_control(name, wt):
        _, ss = run_weights(ts, o, c, wt)
        controls[name] = pack(ss)
        print(f"control {name:28s} CAGR {ss['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  DD {ss['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%  "
              f"Sh {ss['sharpe']:4.2f}")

    add_control("buy_hold_tqqq_sim", wraw)
    # gap only, no confirmation
    wg = build_weights(ts, o, c, r30_th=-1.0)
    add_control("gap_only_no_confirmation", wg)
    # confirmation only, no gap
    wr = build_weights(ts, o, c, gap_th=-1.0)
    add_control("confirmation_only_no_gap", wr)
    # gap but confirmation in the opposite direction (fade)
    gap, r30, full = session_features(ts, o, c, CQ)
    fade_flags = full & np.isfinite(gap) & np.isfinite(r30) & (gap >= GAP_TH) & (r30 < 0)
    add_control("gap_up_r30_down_fade", build_weights(ts, o, c, flags_override=fade_flags))
    # QQQ execution
    add_control("qqq_execution", build_weights(ts, o, c, trade_col=CQ))
    out["controls"] = controls

    # ---- placebos -----------------------------------------------------------
    rng = np.random.default_rng(20261127)
    dates, first, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    full_idx = np.flatnonzero(np.array([int(last[k]) - int(first[k]) == N_BARS - 1
                                        for k in range(len(first))]))
    real_cagr = float(s1["cagr"])
    real_dd = float(s1["max_drawdown"])
    n_sig = int(flags.sum())
    NPL = 200

    cagrs = np.empty(NPL); dds = np.empty(NPL)
    for j in range(NPL):
        pick = rng.choice(full_idx, n_sig, replace=False)
        m = np.zeros(len(first), dtype=bool); m[pick] = True
        _, sj = run_weights(ts, o, c, build_weights(ts, o, c, flags_override=m))
        cagrs[j] = sj["cagr"]; dds[j] = sj["max_drawdown"]
    out["placebo_random_days"] = {
        "n_draws": NPL, "n_events": n_sig, "real_cagr": real_cagr, "real_dd": real_dd,
        "mean_cagr": float(cagrs.mean()), "p95_cagr": float(np.percentile(cagrs, 95)),
        "max_cagr": float(cagrs.max()), "p_value_cagr": float((cagrs >= real_cagr).mean()),
        "mean_dd": float(dds.mean()), "p05_dd": float(np.percentile(dds, 5)),
        "min_dd": float(dds.min()), "dd_percentile": float((dds >= real_dd).mean()),
    }
    print("placebo random days", {k: round(float(v), 4)
                                   for k, v in out["placebo_random_days"].items()})

    cagrs2 = np.empty(NPL); dds2 = np.empty(NPL)
    for j in range(NPL):
        er = rng.integers(30, 60, len(first))   # 10:01..10:30 fill
        _, sj = run_weights(ts, o, c,
                            build_weights(ts, o, c, entry_random=er))
        cagrs2[j] = sj["cagr"]; dds2[j] = sj["max_drawdown"]
    out["placebo_random_entry"] = {
        "n_draws": NPL, "entry_window": "10:01..10:30", "real_cagr": real_cagr,
        "real_dd": real_dd,
        "mean_cagr": float(cagrs2.mean()), "p95_cagr": float(np.percentile(cagrs2, 95)),
        "max_cagr": float(cagrs2.max()), "p_value_cagr": float((cagrs2 >= real_cagr).mean()),
        "mean_dd": float(dds2.mean()), "p05_dd": float(np.percentile(dds2, 5)),
        "dd_percentile": float((dds2 >= real_dd).mean()),
    }
    print("placebo random entry", {k: round(float(v), 4)
                                    for k, v in out["placebo_random_entry"].items()
                                    if isinstance(v, (int, float, np.floating))})

    stale = np.zeros(len(first), dtype=bool)
    stale[1:] = flags[:-1]
    _, sstale = run_weights(ts, o, c, build_weights(ts, o, c, flags_override=stale))
    out["placebo_stale_signal"] = pack(sstale)
    print(f"placebo stale signal  CAGR {sstale['cagr']*100:.2f}%  "
          f"DD {sstale['max_drawdown']*100:.2f}%  Sh {sstale['sharpe']:.2f}")

    # ---- cut tests ----------------------------------------------------------
    cuts = {}
    for year in (2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023):
        cuts[str(year)] = {
            "strategy": calendar_year_cut(res1["ts"], res1["equity"], year),
            "benchmark_ex_year": calendar_year_cut(ts[i0:], c[i0:, CT], year),
        }
    out["cut_tests"] = cuts
    for y, v in cuts.items():
        print(f"cut ex-{y}: strat {v['strategy']['cagr']*100:6.2f}% / "
              f"{v['strategy']['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%  "
              f"bench {v['benchmark_ex_year']['cagr']*100:6.2f}% / "
              f"{v['benchmark_ex_year']['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%")

    # ---- causality: truncation ---------------------------------------------
    j = bt.start_index(ts, "2022-01-03")
    w_trunc = build_weights(ts[:j], o[:j], c[:j])
    out["causality_day_boundary"] = {
        "truncation_date": "2022-01-03",
        "prior_weights_unchanged": bool(np.allclose(w_trunc[:j], w[:j])),
        "max_abs_diff": float(np.max(np.abs(w_trunc[:j] - w[:j]))),
    }
    print("causality day boundary", out["causality_day_boundary"])

    j2 = bt.start_index(ts, "2020-03-12 11:07")
    w_trunc2 = build_weights(ts[:j2], o[:j2], c[:j2])
    n_cmp2 = bt.start_index(ts, "2020-03-12")
    out["causality_intraday_cut"] = {
        "truncation_date": "2020-03-12 11:07",
        "prior_weights_unchanged": bool(np.allclose(w_trunc2[:n_cmp2], w[:n_cmp2])),
        "max_abs_diff": float(np.max(np.abs(w_trunc2[:n_cmp2] - w[:n_cmp2]))),
    }
    print("causality intraday cut", out["causality_intraday_cut"])

    # ---- kill criteria ------------------------------------------------------
    corr_max = max(v["corr"] for v in out["correlations"].values())
    n_pos_sub = sum(1 for v in out["subperiods"].values() if v and v["cagr"] > 0)
    out["kill_criteria"] = [
        {"criterion": "dev CAGR at 1 bp below the 36.72% TQQQ bar",
         "value": float(s1["cagr"]), "threshold": 0.3672,
         "failed": bool(s1["cagr"] < 0.3672)},
        {"criterion": "5 bp CAGR below 0",
         "value": float(results[5.0][1]["cagr"]), "threshold": 0.0,
         "failed": bool(results[5.0][1]["cagr"] < 0.0)},
        {"criterion": "fewer than 30 independent events",
         "value": int(n_events), "threshold": 30,
         "failed": bool(n_events < 30)},
        {"criterion": "fewer than 100 fills",
         "value": int(s1["fills"]), "threshold": 100,
         "failed": bool(s1["fills"] < 100)},
        {"criterion": "fewer than 6 of 8 grid cells positive at 1 bp",
         "value": int(sum(1 for r in grid if r["1bp"]["cagr"] > 0)), "threshold": 6,
         "failed": bool(sum(1 for r in grid if r["1bp"]["cagr"] > 0) < 6)},
        {"criterion": "negative CAGR in 2 or more of 3 subperiods",
         "value": int(3 - n_pos_sub), "threshold": 2,
         "failed": bool(n_pos_sub < 2)},
        {"criterion": "placebo random-day p-value above 0.10",
         "value": float(out["placebo_random_days"]["p_value_cagr"]), "threshold": 0.10,
         "failed": bool(out["placebo_random_days"]["p_value_cagr"] > 0.10)},
        {"criterion": "daily correlation above 0.70 with an existing winner",
         "value": float(corr_max), "threshold": 0.70,
         "failed": bool(corr_max > 0.70)},
        {"criterion": "causality max weight drift above 1e-12",
         "value": float(max(out["causality_day_boundary"]["max_abs_diff"],
                            out["causality_intraday_cut"]["max_abs_diff"])),
         "threshold": 1e-12,
         "failed": bool(max(out["causality_day_boundary"]["max_abs_diff"],
                            out["causality_intraday_cut"]["max_abs_diff"]) > 1e-12)},
    ]
    out["verdict"] = {
        "headline": "positive and robust, but below the above-TQQQ CAGR bar",
        "passed": [k["criterion"] for k in out["kill_criteria"] if not k["failed"]],
        "failed": [k["criterion"] for k in out["kill_criteria"] if k["failed"]],
    }
    for k in out["kill_criteria"]:
        print(f"kill {'FAIL' if k['failed'] else 'pass'}  {k['criterion']}  value={k['value']:.6g}")

    (HERE / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2, default=float))
    print("wrote", HERE / "result.json")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
